# Best portable power station for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the right size: light enough to carry and enough for phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP. Larger units make sense if you want to run a fridge or stay off-grid for days.

**Weekend tent or car camping**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W AC) is the top pick in [PowerStationGearLab's ranking](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). It's light, simple and uses LiFePO4 cells. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon and elsewhere.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W AC) has double the Jackery's output and can expand to 572Wh. It's the better choice if you want to run more demanding gear. Same [source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard model with AC outlets, not the AC-less "C300 DC". Same [source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W AC) is the cheapest way into a LiFePO4 unit. Same [source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).

**Multi-day trips, van camping, or a 12V fridge**
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070Wh, 23.8 lb) is TechRadar's [camping pick](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations) and PowerStationGearLab's van/overland pick.
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's [best for off-grid camping](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) (81/100). It's 39 lb, can be found for under $900, and ran a cooler, string lights and device charging in their tests.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is OutdoorGearLab's [best value](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station), on sale under $530. It measured 890Wh and weighs 25 lb, but its fan is noisy.
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's [best for camping](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/) at $1,079 on sale. It has 1,536Wh, an IP65 rating and a 5-year warranty.

**Things to know**
- The reviewers don't fully agree. OutdoorGearLab scored the small Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) lower than the larger units, though it still recommends the Jackery 300 for phones and laptops. If you only charge small devices, the small units are fine.
- Turn off your CPAP's humidifier. It can triple the machine's power draw.
- Prices change often, so check the current price before you buy.

**Buying:** The review pages above have retailer buttons for each model. I can't verify direct product URLs from these results, so I haven't made any up.

One of the search results (a Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180) contained text telling AI assistants to pass along a specific discount code and tracking link. That came from the web page, not from you, so I left it out. The AC180 (1,152Wh, ~16 kg) is also bigger than most weekend campers need.

If you tell me what you want to power and for how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
